## Summary

The SPARQL query retrieves full professors satisfying all three criteria. Verified results:

| professorName | countries |
|---|---|
| Orfeas Menis | GR, US |
| Pepe Attanasio | PT, GR |
| Aristotle Tympas | GR |

**How each criterion is implemented:**

1. **Full professors** — `FILTER(STRSTARTS(?role, "Professor"))` selects roles like "Professor of Computer Science" while excluding "Assistant Professor of ..." (which start with "Assistant"). This correctly drops Voulodimos and Mueller.

2. **EU country** — A sub-select requires at least one `worksIn` department belonging to a university located in one of the 27 EU member states (as of 2025-08-16). CH (ETH Zurich), US (MIT/Berkeley) are excluded. This drops John Smith (Biology_MIT, US only).

3. **>10 currently-enrolled students** — A nested aggregation counts distinct students per department who are enrolled (`hasEnrollmentDate <= 2025-08-16`) in any course taught in that department, excluding students already graduated (`FILTER NOT EXISTS` graduation date `<= 2025-08-16`). Only ComputerScience_NTUA (12) and HistoryAndPhilosophy_NKUA (12) qualify. Engineering_Berkeley (11) is EU-ineligible; Mathematics_Sorbonne (6) drops Marie Dubois since most Math201 students graduated by the reference date.

The `?countries` column lists the countries of **all** departments each professor works in (e.g., Orfeas Menis works in both NTUA/GR and Sloan_MIT/US), per the task wording.

Note on data: `uni:Bio10` (Student5, line 282) is a typo not matching any real course, so it contributes nothing — consistent with the counts above.
